title: Soldering tools for the desk build
ask: Which of the soldering tools the desk build needs do you already own?
why: You solder the two units' boards yourself at the desk (F3 the Display Unit, F5 the Control Unit). The only soldering row in the record is the iron and solder (P044), with the multimeter (P045), and both sit in the Amazon cart, which is not paid until after the freeze - long after the desk build. About a dozen chips on the two carriers and the panel have a pad underneath (the two 5 V regulators, the motor driver, the power switches, the light driver): an iron cannot reach those, they need solder paste and hot air or a hot plate. No row holds paste, flux, hot air, tweezers or a magnifier. The record does not say what is already on your bench, so the first order may be missing what the build cannot start without, or may buy what you already have.
options:
(a) I own none of it. The iron and solder (P044) and the meter (P045) move from the Amazon cart into the first order, and rows are added for a hot-air station, solder paste, flux, fine tweezers and a magnifier. About 75 USD moved and about 90 to 130 USD added, est. Closes off nothing.
(b) I own an iron, solder and a meter, but nothing for chips with a pad underneath. Rows are added for a hot-air station, solder paste, flux and fine tweezers: about 80 to 110 USD added, est. P044 and P045 are marked in hand and leave the Amazon cart, about 75 USD less there.
(c) I own all of it, hot air or a hot plate included. Nothing is bought; P044 and P045 are marked in hand and leave the Amazon cart, about 75 USD less there.
(d) Something else - say in words what you have and what you lack.
recommend: (a), unless you own any of it - then the option that says what you own; the answer only decides what the first order adds
stops: F3 and F5, the two board builds. The orders Y16 and Y18 do not wait on it.

title: The tach wire's shield on the engine side
ask: Should the shield on the engine side of the tach wire be carried through the spare pin 5 of the engine leg's plug to the node's ground?
why: The tach wire from the coil to the dash is shielded in two pieces that meet at the engine leg's plug at the dash post (L1-S1). The dash-side piece has its shield grounded at the node, as it should. The engine-side piece has its shield cut off at the coil, and at the plug it has nowhere to go: an earlier ruling left cavity 5 of that plug empty, so as the record stands the engine-side shield is connected at neither end and does nothing. The answer decides whether one more pin goes into that plug, and how the step that builds the engine leg (E23) and the step that terminates the PMU connector (E16) read.
options:
(a) Carry the engine-side shield through the spare cavity 5 of the plug and on to the node's ground with the dash-side one: one continuous shield grounded at the node only. Costs one size-16 contact from the kits already on the list; cavity 5 is no longer a spare (it frees again at the LS swap, when the tach wire itself goes).
(b) Ground the engine-side shield at the coil end to the engine instead, and keep the dash-side one at the node: nothing more in the plug; but that shield then references the engine block, which is the noisiest ground in the car.
(c) Drop the shield on the engine side and run a plain wire to the coil: cheapest and simplest; the coil's pulses (hundreds of volts at the negative terminal) then sit unshielded beside the other engine-leg wires.
recommend: (a), unless you want pin 5 of the engine leg's plug kept free before the LS swap
stops: Y47's tach-shield item and so E16 (terminating the PMU connector) and the engine leg's build E23

title: The factory harness after the shakedown
ask: Once the new harness has passed its shakedown, should the boxed factory harness be kept, sold, or stripped for parts?
why: The factory harness comes out of the car whole when the new one goes in and sits in a box until the shakedown has proven the new harness. After that the record has no instruction for it, and the last step of the project (what to keep, what to label, what leaves the garage) cannot be written until you say. Keeping it keeps a way back to the factory car; selling or stripping it closes that way back.
options:
(a) Keep it: labelled, bagged and boxed with the car, the way back to stock and the reference for any factory connector later. Costs a box of shelf space; forecloses nothing.
(b) Sell it once the shakedown is done: some money back; forecloses returning the car to its factory wiring.
(c) Strip it for its factory connectors, terminals and grommets as repair stock, then recycle the rest: keeps the parts most likely to be needed; forecloses a full return to stock.
recommend: (a), unless the shelf space matters more than a way back to stock
stops: Y47's last item and the project's closing steps for the old harness
